Why This Chemistry: Tf Lys residues form amide bonds with surface –COOH (PF-127/succinic anhydride or carboxylated Pluronic). Standard 2-step: activate COOH 4 h RT, add Tf dropwise, couple 4 °C overnight. BCA-confirmed Tf loading; DOX EE 95.7% (Entry 2).
Key Constraint: Activate COOH with EDC/NHS BEFORE Tf addition (15–30 min). Do NOT mix EDC + Tf + NPs simultaneously. Remove excess EDC by ultracentrifuge (93,000 g, 30 min) or quench with 2-ME before coupling. High EDC ratios risk Tf self-crosslinking.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 1: Activate COOH on PF-127-MSN with EDC(1mg/mL)+NHS(1mg/mL), 4h RT. Add Tf dropwise, 4°C overnight. Centrifuge+wash+lyophilize. Entry 2: EDC+NHS 0.25M, stir 15min RT, add 130µg Tf in PBS, overnight. Ultracentrifuge 93,000g 30min to remove unbound Tf. Entry 3: NH2-MSN coated with chitosan or PLGA; Tf via EDC/NHS; pore size 2.5–5.2nm for gemcitabine.

Why This Chemistry: APTS amine surface reacted with SM(PEG)8 to install terminal maleimide. Tf thiolated with TCEP (1:1 molar, 5 min). NP-PEG-Mal + Tf-SH at 1:1 mass ratio, 2h RT 400 rpm. PEG8 spacer reduces steric hindrance. Uptake pathway depends on PEG architecture (Entry 6).
Key Constraint: TCEP 1:1 molar to Tf — do NOT over-reduce (unfolds protein). Quench β-mercaptoethanol 1 mM, 5 min immediately after coupling. Store at 4°C. Maleimide hydrolyses at pH >7.5 — keep at pH 7.4.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
>80% Ab/Tf activity
 retained (Entry 6);
 uptake pathway
 confirmed
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 6: SiNP-NH2 (APTS) → SM(PEG)8 (10×, HEPES pH7.4, 1h). TCEP 1:1 to Tf (5 min). Add NP-PEG-Mal + Tf-SH (1:1 mass), 2h RT 400rpm. Quench β-ME 1mM 5min. Wash 4× PBS. Entry 7: Derivatize Tf Lys with sulfo-SMCC (introduces maleimide); thiolate payload with Traut's (1:1, 0°C, 12h, pH 8.0). WARNING: Traut's can reduce Tf disulfides at high pH—use low conc and 0°C.

Why This Chemistry: Tf grafted via redox-cleavable disulfide bonds — serves as BOTH capping agent AND targeting ligand (Entry 5). GSH in tumor microenvironment triggers Tf detachment + simultaneous drug release. Eliminates need for separate cap and ligand.
Key Constraint: Disulfide NOT stable in systemic circulation (plasma GSH ~5 µM). Use ONLY for intracellular GSH-triggered release. Not suitable if blood-stable conjugate required.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
Redox-responsive
 release confirmed;
 quantitative CE not
 reported (Entry 5)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 5: Tf grafted via disulfide bonds to MSN surface using cystamine dihydrochloride linker. Tf acts as dual capping + targeting agent. GSH-triggered release in tumor microenvironment confirmed. FTIR + DLS characterization.

Why This Chemistry: 8arm-PEG-COOH (10 kDa) conjugated to DHA; EDC(4mg)+NHS(6mg) activate terminal COOH; 8mg Tf in PBS coupled RT 6h then dialyzed MWCO 30kDa (Entry 4). PLGA-PEG-COOH terminus used for Tf variant (oxalate) — oxalate variant showed 3× lower IC50 vs native Tf (Entry 17).
Key Constraint: PEGylation can bury –COOH groups. Verify accessible carboxyl density before coupling. Dialysis (MWCO 30kDa, 12h) required to remove free Tf (Entry 4). For PLGA-PEG systems, activate at MES pH 6 then transfer to PBS pH 7.4 for coupling.
Critical pH Range:
~7.4 PBS
 (activation + coupling);
 MES pH 6 → PBS 7.4
 (for PLGA-PEG)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 4: Dissolve 50mg PEG-conjugate in 10mL PBS. Add EDC(4mg)+NHS(6mg), stir RT 15min. Add 8mg Tf in 5mL PBS, stir RT 6h. Dialyze MWCO 30kDa vs PBS 12h. Lyophilize. Entry 17: PLGA-PEG-Tf NPs in 3D PLGA scaffolds; oxalate Tf variant > native Tf. Entry 18: Non-covalent Tf adsorption on PLGA (simpler but less stable — included as comparator).

Why This Chemistry: Tf thiolated with Traut's 5× excess (HEPES pH 8). Tf-SH coupled to MB-DOPE micelles (1:10 protein:lipid, 37°C, 1h). Post-inserted into drug-loaded PLGA NPs (37°C, 1h). IC50 0.77–1.21 nM (Tf-NP) vs 1.90–3.41 nM non-targeted (Entry 19).
Key Constraint: MBS-DOPE synthesis required first (MBS + DOPE in CHCl3 + TEA, overnight RT). Traut's 5× at pH 8 — risk of Tf disulfide reduction at higher ratios. Post-insertion at 37°C ≤1h to avoid lipid phase artefacts.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 19: (1) Synthesize MB-DOPE (MBS+DOPE in CHCl3+TEA, overnight RT). (2) Form micelles. (3) Thiolate Tf (5× Traut's, HEPES pH 8, 1h). (4) Mix Tf-SH with MB-DOPE micelles 1:10 protein:lipid, 37°C, 1h. (5) Post-insert Tf-DOPE into drug-loaded PLGA NPs, 37°C, 1h. Characterized by DLS, zeta, HPLC, aromatase inhibition.

Why This Chemistry: PLGA 50:50 provides terminal –COOH without modification. Activate with EDC (20× molar excess), agitate RT 30min, add Tf (2× excess), agitate 1h RT (Entry 14). Target ~100 Tf/NP. BCA quantification of unbound Tf in supernatant confirms loading. Enhanced uptake in cancer cells vs non-targeted.
Key Constraint: EDC 20× molar excess needed for sufficient activation. Quantify unbound Tf by BCA (supernatant method). CMC-coated PLGA (Entry 16): activate with EDC 2mM + NHS 5mM in NaCl pH 5.5, 15min; quench with 2-mercaptoethanol 20mM before adding Tf.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 14: Activate PLGA-COOH with EDC (20× excess), agitate RT 30min. Add Tf (2× excess), agitate 1h RT. Centrifuge, resuspend in water. BCA quantification. Entry 15: Double emulsification → PLGA NPs → EDC/NHS coupling with Tf. Confirmed by TEM/SEM/FTIR. Enhanced intranasal brain uptake in rats. Entry 16: CMC-COOH surface. EDC 2mM + NHS 5mM in NaCl pH 5.5, 15min. Quench with 2-ME 20mM. Centrifuge 1000rpm 10min 4°C. Then add Tf.

Why This Chemistry: Tf thiolated with Traut's (1:5 or 3:1 protein:Traut). Coupled to DSPE-PEG2000-Mal micelles then post-inserted into preformed liposomes (Entries 8,9) OR DSPE-PEG-Mal incorporated during formation + Tf coupled post-extrusion (Entry 10). DOX EE 95% (Entry 8). EE ERN 68.5% (Entry 9). >90% DSPE-PEG-Mal retained by Ellman's (Entry 10).
Key Constraint: Traut's ratio critical: 1:5 (Entry 8) or 3:1 (Entry 10) — higher ratios risk reducing Tf disulfides. Quench β-mercaptoethanol 15min after coupling. Thermal equilibration at 55°C 1h for post-insertion (Entry 10) — do NOT exceed 1h.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 8: Thiolate Tf (Traut 1:5 RT). Couple Tf-SH to DSPE-PEG2000-Mal micelles. Post-insert into DOX liposomes. IC50 decreased 68.7% vs plain. Entry 9: Tf-SH + Mal-mPEG2000-DSPE → post-insert into LP-ERN at 100:1 lipid:conjugate, 37°C, 30min. Entry 10: Add DSPE-PEG-Mal (25mg/mL DMSO) at 1mol%, 55°C 1h. Thiolate Tf (Traut 3:1, 1h). Couple 1:1 DSPE:Tf, overnight 4°C. Quench β-ME 15min. Entry 12: Ab:DSPE-PEG-Mal 1:10, 4°C 4h stirring; ultracentrifuge 55,000rpm 1h.

Why This Chemistry: Landmark Huwyler/Pardridge 1996 BBB immunoliposome protocol. OX26 mAb thiolated at very low Traut's ratio (1:40 mAb:Traut) to limit to ~1 thiol/mAb. ~10% coupling efficiency; ~30 Ab/liposome optimal for brain delivery. Enhanced pharmacokinetics in rats confirmed.
Key Constraint: mAb:Traut 1:40 — lower than for other Abs (prevents >1 thiol/mAb from aggregating). Coupling efficiency not affected by mAb concentration at 100–400:1 phospholipid:mAb ratio. Exchange buffer to phosphate pH 8.0 before coupling. Separate on Sephadex CL-4B.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 11/34: Thiolate OX26 mAb (Traut's 1:40, 0.15M Na-borate + 0.1mM EDTA pH 8.5, 60min RT). Ellman's: avg 1 thiol/mAb. Exchange to 0.1M Na-phosphate pH 8.0. React immediately with DSPE-PEG-Mal liposomes overnight RT. Separate on Sephadex CL-4B. Radiolabeling (3H-cholesterol) for PK in rats.

NP Type:
Silica NP
 (APTES-NH2, carboxylated
 SiO2, ORMOSIL-PEG,
 ~30–150 nm)
Why This Chemistry: APTES-functionalized SiNPs → EDC/NHS couples Ab Lys residues to NP –COOH or installs COOH via PEG2000-COOH (Entry 25). ORMOSIL-PEG-COOH: activate with EDC/Sulfo-NHS MES pH 6 (15min), desalt, add cetuximab in PBS pH 7.4, 2h RT (Entry 25). ~262.5 ng Ab per 3mg NPs (Entry 22). CE 1–20% typical for random Lys coupling.
Key Constraint: Use Sulfo-NHS (water-soluble) not NHS for NP-surface activation. Activate NP-COOH FIRST, desalt, THEN add Ab — do NOT mix EDC + Ab + NPs simultaneously. Two-buffer protocol (MES pH 6 activation → PBS pH 7.4 coupling) maximizes NHS-ester stability.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
CE 1–20%
 (random Lys coupling,
 Entry 29);
 ~262.5 ng Ab/3mg NP
 (Entry 22)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 22: APTES-SiNPs (~45nm) + EDC/NHS in 0.9% NaCl, 12h coupling. Entry 25: Synthesize ORMOSIL (APTS+VPTES in AOT/DMSO/water microemulsion). PEGylate with PEG2000-COOH. Activate COOH (EDC/Sulfo-NHS, MES pH 6, 15min). Desalt. Add cetuximab in PBS pH 7.4, 2h RT. Wash by centrifugation. Entry 29: SiO2-COOH NPs 1mg/mL; EDC 0.4mg + Sulfo-NHS 1.1mg in MES pH 6, 30min; PBS pH 7.4; cetuximab 25µg/mg NP, 1–2h RT; quench hydroxylamine 10mM 10min.

Recommended Chemistry:
Maleimide–thiol
 (dual PEGylation +
 TCEP or Traut's
 thiolation)
Why This Chemistry: Two-step PEGylation on mSiO2: Mal-PEG5k-NH2 for surface amine, then Mal-PEG5k-SCM for terminal maleimide. TCEP reduces TRC105 disulfides → Ellman's confirms –SH. React TRC105-SH with NP-PEG-Mal, 2h RT. ~17.5% ID/g tumor at 24h by PET (Entry 23). 9-month lyophilized stability maintained (Entry 24).
Key Constraint: TCEP reduction must be confirmed by Ellman's assay before coupling. Quench β-mercaptoethanol 1mM after coupling. TCEP-reduced Ab must be used IMMEDIATELY — thiols re-oxidize within 30–60min. Add 2mM EDTA to all buffers.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 23/26: Thiolate mSiO2 with MPS at 86–90°C ethanol. PEGylate with Mal-PEG5k-NH2 overnight RT. Install NOTA then Mal-PEG5k-SCM. TCEP-reduce TRC105, react with NP-PEG-Mal 2h RT. Entry 24: MSNP-PEI (4:1 mass PEI); cross-link DSP 40min; Mal-PEG5k-NHS (1:1) in PBS pH 7.2 2h; Traut's 50× to trastuzumab pH 8.0 2h; Ab-SH + MSNP-PEI-PEG overnight 4°C. Entry 27: SM(PEG)8 (10×, HEPES pH 7.4, 1h). TCEP 1:1 Ab, 5min. 1:1 mass coupling 2h RT 400rpm. Quench β-ME 1mM.

Why This Chemistry: Bioorthogonal click: PEI-MSNP azide-functionalized via NHS-PEG4-N3 (borate pH 8.5, 4h). Ab DBCO-labelled via DBCO-PEG4-NHS (10eq, borate pH 8.5, 6h). Purify DBCO-Ab on Zeba 40K. Mix DBCO-Ab (100µg) with N3-NP (10mg/mL), overnight RT (Entry 28). Specific uptake in EGFR+ A431 cells; no uptake in EGFR− HEK293.
Key Constraint: DBCO labelling: avoid >15 DBCO/Ab (causes aggregation). Zeba spin-column purification required to remove excess DBCO-PEG4-NHS before NP mixing. Click reaction overnight RT (slower than thiol-maleimide 2h). Borate buffer pH 8.5 for all NHS steps.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
Functional uptake
 confirmed in EGFR+
 cells; quantitative CE
 not reported (Entry 28)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 28: Coat MSNP with 0.75% PEI (pH 7, 1:1, 3h). Add NHS-PEG4-N3 (1.5mg in DMSO) in borate pH 8.5, stir 4h. Centrifuge. Label Ab with DBCO-PEG4-NHS (10eq, borate pH 8.5, 6h). Purify on Zeba 40K. Mix DBCO-Ab (100µg) with N3-NP (450µL × 10mg/mL), overnight RT. Centrifuge, wash. DOX released in acidic lysosomes confirmed by confocal.

NP Type:
PLGA NP / PLGA-PEG NP
 (bare PLGA-COOH or
 PLGA-PEG-NHS,
 ~105–128 nm)
Recommended Chemistry:
EDC/NHS
 (amide bond,
 PLGA terminal –COOH
 or PLGA-PEG-NHS)
Why This Chemistry: Direct PLGA –COOH activation. MES pH 6 activation (30min) → PBS pH 7.4 coupling (2h RT). Cetuximab 25µg/mg NP (Entry 39: CE ~40%; Entry 40: CE 39.77±3.4%). PLGA-PEG-NHS NPs couple Ab primary amine directly (Entry 38, anti-TNFR2). In vivo tumor growth inhibition confirmed in MC38 colon cancer model.
Key Constraint: CE ~40% for random Lys coupling. Use Sulfo-NHS not NHS for water-soluble activation. Quench excess EDC with 2-ME BEFORE Tf/Ab addition (Entry 16-type) to prevent crosslinking. At high Ab concentrations: use dilute conditions to avoid inter-NP crosslinking (Entry 37 note).
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 39: TMZ-PLGA NPs by single emulsion. Activate COOH with EDC+Sulfo-NHS in MES pH 6.0, 30min RT. Exchange to PBS pH 7.4. Add cetuximab 25µg/mg NP, stir 2h RT. Centrifuge, wash 3× PBS. Entry 40: Same protocol; CE 39.77±3.4%; zeta −31.0±0.8mV. Entry 38: PLGA-PEG-NHS NPs + anti-TNFR2 in PBS pH 7.4, 2h RT, wash 3×. Entry 21: f(ab')2 fragments gave 26–47% CE vs 7–15% for full IgG — prefer fragments for efficiency.

Ligand Type:
Antibody (full IgG
 or f(ab')2 fragment)
 (anti-FZD7, anti-CD8a,
 anti-CD133)
Recommended Chemistry:
Maleimide–thiol
 (TCEP or DTT reduction
 + NP-PEG-Mal surface)
Why This Chemistry: TCEP 100× to Ab → ~4 free thiols/Ab confirmed by Ellman's (Entry 41). High loading: 1,063±97 Ab/NP vs 192 Ab/NP at low loading. IdeS protease → f(ab')2 → DTT 10mM exposes hinge –SH for site-selective coupling (Entry 42). Maleimide method: 99% Ab retained at 5 days vs 84% for EDC/NHS (Entry 42). sulfo-SMCC installs maleimide on PLGA-PEG-NH2 NPs (Entry 43).
Key Constraint: PLGA-PEG-Mal NPs must be freshly prepared — maleimide groups hydrolyse at pH >7. Verify maleimide availability by Ellman's before coupling. Use PBS + 2mM EDTA to prevent thiol oxidation. TCEP-reduced Ab must react immediately with NPs.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 41: TCEP 100× to Ab, PBS+2mM EDTA, 4°C overnight. Mix Ab-SH with PLGA-PEG-Mal NPs. Purify by centrifugation. Ellman's + ELISA confirmation. Entry 42: IdeS protease cleaves Ab → f(ab')2. DTT 10mM (2.5µL per 100µg Ab). Desalt 7kDa MWCO. 2h coupling 25°C shaking. 5-day stability: 99% Ab retained. Entry 43: Sulfo-SMCC (10× molar, PBS pH 7.4, 1h) installs maleimide on PLGA-PEG-NH2. Traut's 1:5 to anti-CD133 Ab (1h). Ab-SH + NP-Mal (25µg/mg NP, PBS+EDTA, 2h RT).

Ligand Type:
Antibody (full IgG
 or VHH/Fab' fragment)
 (trastuzumab, cetuximab,
 anti-HER2 VHH)
Recommended Chemistry:
Maleimide–thiol
 (Traut's 3:1 or TCEP
 + DSPE-PEG2000-Mal;
 post-insertion or
 during formation)
Why This Chemistry: Standard immunoliposome method. DSPE-PEG2000-Mal at 0.5–1mol% provides PEG stealth + reactive maleimide. Traut's 3:1 (protein:Traut) introduces –SH on Ab. Couple overnight 4°C. EE ~90% rapamycin (Entry 30). ~30 Ab/liposome optimal (Entry 32). Bispecific VHH-liposomes: 10-fold uptake increase (Entry 33). Fab' fragment via 2-MEA reduction (Entry 36).
Key Constraint: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal post-insertion: 55°C, 1h (Entry 35) — verify Mal retention >90% by Ellman's. Traut's 3:1 for trastuzumab/cetuximab (Entries 30, 32, 35). For Fab' fragments use 2-MEA 10mM 37°C 90min instead (Entry 36). Purify by SEC (Sephadex CL-4B) or ultrafiltration MWCO 100kDa to remove unbound Ab.
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 30: Thin-film hydration/extrusion (DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal 56:39:0.5–1mol). Traut's 3:1 1h RT. Couple overnight 4°C. Wash MWCO 100kDa. Entry 32: Same; Sephadex CL-4B cleanup. ~30 Ab/liposome. Entry 33: HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal 56:38:3:3mol. Engineered Cys-VHH, TCEP 30min, couple 2h RT. Entry 35: Post-insert DSPE-PEG-Mal (25mg/mL DMSO, 1mol%) at 55°C 1h. Entry 36: Pepsin digest → F(ab')2. 2-MEA 10mM 37°C 90min → Fab'-SH. React with DSPE-PEG-Mal micelles 1:1, 2h RT. Post-insert 37°C 30min.

Why This Chemistry: DSPE-PEG2000-COOH (1mol%) activated with EDC(10×)+Sulfo-NHS(25×) in PBS pH 6, 15min. Quench excess EDC with 2-mercaptoethanol (20mM). Add trastuzumab 1:10 Ab:lipid molar ratio, PBS pH 7.4, 2h RT. CE 20–45%. Dialyze vs PBS (MWCO 300kDa) to remove unbound Ab (Entry 37).
Key Constraint: Risk of inter-liposome crosslinking with EDC/NHS at high Ab concentrations — use dilute conditions. Dialysis cleanup required (MWCO <1,000kDa Float-A-Lyzer). EDC/NHS less preferred than Mal-thiol for liposomes — crosslinking risk and random orientation.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
CE 20–45%
 (Entry 37);
 higher crosslinking
 risk at high [Ab]
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 37: Prepare DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000-COOH liposomes. Activate COOH with EDC(10×)+Sulfo-NHS(25×), PBS pH 6, 15min. Quench excess EDC with 2-ME (20mM). Add trastuzumab at 1:10 Ab:lipid molar ratio, PBS pH 7.4, 2h RT. Dialyze vs PBS (MWCO 300kDa). Risk of crosslinking: use dilute conditions.

Ligand Type:
RGD / cRGD Peptide
 (linear GRGDS,
 cyclic cRGDfK, cRGDfc,
 cRGDfC, RGD-NAMs)
NP Type:
Silica NP / MSN
 (APTES-NH2,
 thiol-MSN,
 vinyl-MSN, ~100–200 nm)
Recommended Chemistry:
Maleimide–thiol
 (Mal-PEG12-NHS on
 MSN-NH2 + Cys-RGD
 free thiol)
Why This Chemistry: Two-step: (1) React MSN-NH2 with Mal-PEG12-NHS → MSN-PEGmal. (2) Conjugate Cys-RGD-FAM via thiol-maleimide click. Tune RGD density by adjusting peptide:MSN ratio. High density: 29.1 nmol RGD/mg MSN; Low: 14.5 nmol/mg (Entry 47). PEG12 spacer provides antifouling layer and controls surface density precisely.
Key Constraint: Maleimide hydrolyses above pH 7.5 — keep coupling buffer at pH 7.4 or below. Thiol-disulfide (Entry 48): MSN-SH activated with 2,2'-DTP then react with Cys-cRGD — different chemistry in same paper vs Tf-epoxide (Entry 48, Ferris 2011). Tune surface density by peptide:NP ratio.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
High density:
 29.1 nmol RGD/mg MSN;
 Low density:
 14.5 nmol/mg
 (Entry 47 by fluorescence)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 47: (1) React MSN-NH2 with Mal-PEG12-NHS → MSN-PEGmal. (2) Conjugate Cys-RGD-FAM via thiol-maleimide at pH 7.4. FAM fluorescence quantifies RGD density. Entry 48 (disulfide): MSN-SH (3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane) → 2,2'-DTP activation → react with Cys-cRGD. Entry 46: HA+RGD dual targeting via EDC/NHS on GNRs@mSiO2-NH2 surface. DOX loaded with pH-enzyme + NIR-triggered release. Entry 44 (PAA surface): MES pH 6 activation 30min, borate pH 8.0 coupling 16h at 25°C — 78% efficiency gain. Entry 49: thermo+pH responsive pNIBIm-AA-RGD copolymer on vinyl-MSN.

Ligand Type:
RGD / cRGD Peptide
 (linear GRGDS,
 cyclic cRGDfK)
Recommended Chemistry:
Maleimide–thiol
 (Mal-PEG-PLGA surface
 + Cys-RGD free thiol,
 HEPES pH 7.0)
Why This Chemistry: KEY REFERENCE (Entry 58, Martínez-Jothar 2018): 84±4% CE at 2:1 Mal:thiol molar ratio, 30min, HEPES pH 7.0. Best NP prep method and storage (4°C > −20°C) also optimized. IAASF technique (Entry 60): PLA-PEG-MAL at emulsion oil–water interface → Mal displayed on NP surface without post-modification. NMR confirms coupling (maleimide proton peak disappears). 2–3× uptake increase; ~2× tumor AUC in vivo.
Alternative Chemistry:
EDC/NHS
 (PLGA-COOH or
 PLGA-PEG-COOH,
 Entries 56, 57;
 lower selectivity)
Key Constraint: Optimal Mal:thiol = 2:1 (Entry 58); excess thiol (>1:1) causes NP crosslinking. Maleimide availability lower than expected due to PEG-PLGA miscibility burying some Mal groups — verify by Ellman's before coupling. Storage at 4°C preferred over −20°C for Mal-PEG-PLGA NPs.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
84±4% CE
 (2:1 Mal:thiol, 30min,
 Entry 58);
 CE 40–70%
 (density-dependent,
 Entry 59);
 2–3× uptake increase
 (Entry 60)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 58 (key): Dissolve cRGDfK in HEPES pH 7.0. Mix with Mal-PEG-PLGA NPs at 2:1 Mal:thiol molar ratio. React RT 30min. Quantify free cRGD in supernatant by HPLC. Entry 59: 3 cRGD densities (1:10, 1:5, 1:2 cRGD:Mal) tested under physiological flow (300 s⁻¹). Entry 60 (IAASF): Add PLA-PEG-MAL during PLGA emulsification. NMR confirms coupling. ~2× tumor AUC in vivo (4T1 model). Entry 56/57: Standard EDC/NHS on PLGA-COOH or PLGA-PEG-COOH in MES pH 6.0–6.5, 2–4h RT.

Ligand Type:
RGD / cRGD Peptide
 (cyclic cRGDfK, cRGDfc,
 cRGDfC, DSPE-PEG-RGD)
NP Type:
Liposome / LNP
 (SPC/Chol/DSPE-PEG-Mal,
 HSPC/Chol/MBPE,
 DLin-MC3-DMA LNP,
 ~80–200 nm)
Why This Chemistry: Cys-RGD reacts directly with DSPE-PEG2000-Mal — no activation step. 98% CE (Entry 51): couple cRGD to liposome maleimide FIRST, then post-insert DSPE-PEG2000 (sequence critical). MALDI-TOF: quantitative 1:1 DSPE-PEG:RGD coupling confirmed (MW increase = RGD-SH MW, Entry 55). LNP (Entry 61): formulate with 0.5mol% DSPE-PEG-Mal; add Cys-peptide in DMF 1.2× excess; react 2h RT; quench with free L-Cys; 0.5mol% cRGD optimal for transfection.
Key Constraint: CRITICAL SEQUENCE (Entry 51): couple cRGD BEFORE PEG post-insertion — reverse gives steric blocking of maleimide, CE drops to <20%. Keep under argon/dark (Entry 50) to prevent thiol oxidation. EDTA in buffer prevents metal-catalysed oxidation. pH 6.5 HEPES for Entry 52 (lower than standard).
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 51 (optimal): (1) Prepare liposomes. (2) Load DOX (ammonium sulfate gradient). (3) Couple cRGD to MBPE-maleimide. (4) Post-insert DSPE-PEG2000. 98% CE. Entry 50: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal in PBS pH 7.2+NaCl+EDTA+TEA; add 2 equiv cRGD; react argon, RT, dark, 12h. Dialyze MWCO 1kDa. Entry 52: cRGD (1mg/mL HEPES pH 6.5) + LCL suspension at 1:10 cRGD:maleimide, overnight. Entry 55: MALDI-TOF confirmed quantitative 1:1 coupling. Entry 61 (LNP/PCT): microfluidics formulation with 0.5mol% DSPE-PEG-Mal. Add Cys-peptide in DMF (1.2× excess). React 2h RT. Quench free L-Cys. Purify 30kDa or 300kDa centrifugal filters.

Why This Chemistry: EDC/HBTU combination for sterically hindered protected peptides in mixed aqueous/organic solvent (water:DMSO 1:1). HBTU activates COOH more efficiently than NHS for protected peptides. Activate DOTA-COOH with EDC/HBTU (5 equiv) 10min, add protected peptide (6 equiv), stir 18h RT. Evaporate solvents. Deprotect side chains with TFA 2h RT (Entry 45).
Alternative Chemistry:
EDC/NHS
 (aqueous only;
 for unprotected
 hydrophilic peptides)
Key Constraint: TFA deprotection step (2h RT) required after coupling — confirm complete deprotection by MS. DMSO co-solvent (1:1 v/v) necessary for peptide solubility; validate NP stability in DMSO before use. Not suitable for base-labile NP coatings.
Typical Efficiency Range (%):
Functional PDT+MRI
 theranostic confirmed;
 quantitative CE not
 reported (Entry 45)
Key Finding / Protocol Notes: Entry 45: Activate DOTA-COOH on NP with EDC+HBTU (5 equiv each) in water/DMSO 1:1 v/v, 10min RT. Add protected ATWLPPR peptide (6 equiv), stir 18h RT. Evaporate solvents. Deprotect side chains with TFA 2h RT. Wash cycles to remove TFA/DMSO. Functional PDT+MRI theranostic NPs confirmed by TEM, DLS, MRI relaxivity, singlet oxygen assay.
